neighbours.label: object/possessive pronoun (him, his, their, your) directly after a verb or preposition in narrative or instructional prose
fire: When the storm finally ended, she ran outside and hugged him tightly.
The old farmer said nothing, but the dog followed him all the way home.
After the meeting, the manager thanked the staff for their patience.
Before you leave the car, always check your mirrors twice.
The coach looked at the young striker and told him to rest.
Once the soldiers had gone, the boy went back to his mother.
Nobody in the village trusted him after the fire at the mill.
Every evening the children wrote letters to their grandparents.
quiet: When the storm finally ended, she ran outside and hugged the tree tightly.
The old farmer said nothing, but the dog followed the cart all the way home.
After the meeting, the manager thanked the staff for the patience shown.
Before anyone leaves the car, always check the mirrors twice.
The coach looked at the young striker and said rest was needed.
Once the soldiers had gone, the boy went back to the farmhouse.
Nobody in the village trusted the baker after the fire at the mill.
Every evening the children wrote letters to distant cousins.
